overview: Archer-Daniels-Midland is one of the world's largest agricultural supply chain managers and processors, originating, transporting, storing, and processing crops (soybeans, corn, wheat, and other oilseeds/grains) into food, feed, industrial, and fuel ingredients. The company is also a leading global provider of human and animal nutrition ingredients, spanning flavors, proteins, and specialty food/feed additives. ADM operates in roughly 75 countries through three reporting segments — Ag Services & Oilseeds, Carbohydrate Solutions, and Nutrition — and is one of the four dominant global grain traders (the 'ABCD' companies: ADM, Bunge, Cargill, Louis Dreyfus) that together handle roughly half of world agricultural trade.

business_model.summary: ADM makes money primarily by buying, storing, transporting, and processing (crushing/milling) agricultural commodities and selling the resulting ingredients (oils, meals, starches, sweeteners, ethanol, feed, and specialty nutrition ingredients) at a margin over input costs — a scale/logistics and commodity-processing business rather than a branded consumer model. Revenue is heavily commodity-price-linked and transactional/volume-driven (crush margins, freight, merchandising spreads) in Ag Services & Oilseeds and Carbohydrate Solutions, with a smaller but higher-margin, more differentiated Nutrition segment (flavors, proteins, specialty ingredients) that behaves more like a branded B2B ingredients business with longer-term customer relationships. The 2026 fiscal year has seen a sharp earnings recovery driven by strong biofuel-linked crush margins: Q3 2026 revenue was $22.3B (up ~10% YoY) with net earnings of $821M (vs. $108M in Q3 2025) and adjusted EPS of $1.77 (vs. $0.92); total segment operating profit of $1.38B was up 64% YoY, led by a 105% jump in Ag Services & Oilseeds and a 40% increase in Carbohydrate Solutions, while Nutrition grew only 3% as soft Human Nutrition/liquid sweetener volumes offset a 21% gain in Animal Nutrition.

revenue_streams.name: Ag Services & Oilseeds (origination, crushing, refining, biodiesel/renewable diesel feedstocks)
revenue_streams.trend: strong on crush margins and biofuel demand, though easing modestly off Q2 2026 peaks

revenue_streams.name: Carbohydrate Solutions (corn/wheat milling, starches, sweeteners, ethanol, Vantage Corn Processors)
revenue_streams.trend: growing, boosted by 45Z tax credit and ethanol/Vantage demand

revenue_streams.name: Nutrition (human nutrition — flavors, proteins, specialty ingredients; animal nutrition — feed additives)
revenue_streams.trend: mixed — Animal Nutrition improving (+21% Q3 2026), Human Nutrition soft on liquid sweetener volumes/margins

revenue_streams.name: Other (corporate, financial services, insurance, Wilmar equity earnings)
revenue_streams.trend: stable to improving; Wilmar equity earnings up ~38% YoY in Q3 2026

business_model.customer_type: Primarily B2B — food, beverage, animal feed, biofuel, and industrial manufacturers; customer base ranges from global CPG/food companies to farmers (origination) and biofuel refiners
business_model.geographic_mix: Global operations in ~75 countries; North America is the largest revenue and profit base (origination, crushing, ethanol), with significant activity in South America (Brazil origination), Europe, and Asia-Pacific (notably China as a major soybean/ag-commodity export destination and a growth market for flavors)

competitive_position.market_position: One of the 'ABCD' oligopoly of global grain traders that together control roughly half of world agricultural commodity trade; ADM is typically the #2 or #3 player by processing volume behind Cargill (private) and roughly on par with Bunge, with a differentiated, though still underperforming, Nutrition ingredients business that most pure commodity traders lack.

moat_factors.description: Extensive network of grain elevators, crushing plants, rail, barge, and port assets built over more than a century provides cost and reliability advantages that are extremely difficult and capital-intensive to replicate.

Integration from farm-gate origination through processing to end-ingredient production captures margin at multiple points in the value chain and provides flexibility to shift capacity toward the highest-margin outputs (e.g., biofuel feedstocks vs. food-grade oil).

Exposure to soybeans, corn, wheat, and other oilseeds across multiple continents and end markets (food, feed, fuel, industrial) smooths some of the volatility inherent in any single commodity or region.

Flavors, proteins, and specialty ingredients carry higher margins and stickier customer relationships than commodity trading, though the segment remains a minority of profit, grew only 3% in Q3 2026, and was the site of the 2024 accounting scandal.

moat_factors.factor: Oligopoly structure / high barriers to entry
moat_factors.description: The capital intensity, regulatory complexity, and scale required to compete in global grain origination and crushing limits new entrants, though state-backed players (COFCO) and private rivals (Cargill, Louis Dreyfus) are well-capitalized incumbents, not new entrants.

weaknesses: Thin, volatile margins inherent to commodity processing — earnings are highly sensitive to crush spreads, freight rates, and government biofuel policy rather than being driven by pricing power; management itself flagged in Q3 2026 that biofuel margins may have peaked for the cycle

Reputational and internal-controls damage from the 2024 Nutrition segment accounting scandal and subsequent SEC enforcement action (settled January 2026 for $40M), which forced restatements and a management/CFO shake-up

Nutrition segment growth remains inconsistent — Q2 2026 showed a 51% operating-profit jump but Q3 2026 growth slowed to just 3%, with Human Nutrition actually declining ~3% on soft liquid sweetener volumes/margins — underscoring the segment's continued underperformance versus targets and peers (Kerry, IFF, Givaudan)

Heavy reliance on government policy (RFS/RVO biofuel mandates, 45Z tax credits, trade policy with China) for a meaningful share of profitability — a political/regulatory tailwind that can reverse, and the stock has already sold off (down roughly 7-12% in the weeks around and after Q3 2026 earnings) on investor concern about how dependent the 2026 earnings beat is on biofuel policy durability
Environmental/operational risk exposure, illustrated by the Decatur, Illinois carbon sequestration well leak and subsequent EPA enforcement order (finalized August 2025)

growth_drivers: Record 2026-2027 Renewable Volume Obligations (RVOs) announced by EPA in March 2026 — the highest biomass-based diesel mandates in the Renewable Fuel Standard's 20-year history — driving soybean oil demand and crush margins into 2027
45Z clean fuel production tax credit continuing to support ethanol plant economics across North America, a key driver behind Carbohydrate Solutions' 40% operating-profit growth in Q3 2026
Wilmar equity-method earnings up ~38% YoY in Q3 2026, adding a growing non-segment profit contribution
Animal Nutrition turnaround (+21% operating profit in Q3 2026) following 2025 portfolio actions and operational improvements, even as Human Nutrition lags

Low-capital-intensity crush capacity expansion: North American crushing debottlenecking projects with roughly one-fourth the capital intensity of greenfield builds, offering high incremental returns, alongside a trimmed FY2026 capex plan ($1.2-$1.3B, down from $1.3-$1.5B) reflecting capital discipline

Carbon capture/carbon markets: entry into the voluntary carbon removal market (announced September 2026) monetizing 800,000+ tons/year of sequestration capacity at the Columbus, Nebraska complex via Puro.earth-certified credits
Continued China demand for North American soybeans supporting origination and crush volumes
53+ consecutive years of dividend increases and an ongoing capital return program signal confidence in through-cycle cash generation

business.description: Core Ag Services & Oilseeds and Carbohydrate Solutions profitability is directly exposed to crop prices, crush spreads, and freight rates; CEO Juan Luciano said on the Q3 2026 call that biofuel/crush margins may have peaked for this cycle even as he expects them to remain historically strong into 2027, leaving forward earnings durability uncertain.

Following the 2024 accounting scandal, the Nutrition segment must rebuild credibility with investors; growth has been uneven — Q2 2026 operating profit rose 51% but Q3 2026 growth slowed to 3% with Human Nutrition down ~3% on soft liquid sweetener demand — showing the turnaround is not yet consistent.
Large trade counterparties, government buyers, and geopolitical shifts in export flows (e.g., China soybean purchasing decisions) can materially move volumes and margins with limited warning.
Droughts, floods, and other weather events affecting corn/soybean/wheat harvests in North and South America directly affect origination volumes and input costs.

financial.description: Net debt/EBITDA and interest coverage remain moderate but not low for a cyclical, thin-margin business; a reversal in crush margins from current elevated levels would pressure coverage ratios.

Net earnings swung from $108M (Q3 2025) to $821M (Q3 2026) — roughly 7.6x — illustrating how policy and margin-environment shifts can swing quarterly earnings dramatically, complicating valuation and guidance reliability even as full-year guidance has now been raised three times in 2026.

financial.risk: Working capital and inventory commodity exposure
financial.description: Large inventories of agricultural commodities carry mark-to-market and financing risk as prices swing, and structured trade finance activities add balance-sheet complexity.

regulatory.risk: SEC enforcement resolved but litigation risk remains
regulatory.description: ADM settled with the SEC in January 2026, paying a $40M civil penalty without admitting or denying wrongdoing, and the DOJ dropped its parallel criminal probe; however, former CFO Vikram Luthar faces a litigated SEC fraud action, and shareholder class-action lawsuits alleging ADM misled investors about Nutrition segment performance remain ongoing.

A material and growing share of 2026 earnings upside is tied to EPA Renewable Volume Obligations and the 45Z tax credit; management itself flagged that biofuel margins may have peaked, and these policies are subject to political change, future rulemakings, and potential legal challenges — a rollback would directly reduce crush margins and ethanol/biodiesel economics heading into 2027.

EPA finalized an enforcement order in August 2025 after a CO2 leak at ADM's Decatur, Illinois carbon sequestration well; the company has since restarted injection under EPA oversight, but the episode highlights operational and reputational risk in its emerging carbon capture business.
As a major exporter/importer of agricultural commodities, ADM is exposed to shifts in U.S.-China trade relations, tariffs, and retaliatory measures affecting soybean and grain export volumes.
Periodic public and political scrutiny of concentration among the four dominant global grain traders creates low-probability but high-impact regulatory tail risk.

macro.description: ADM's core earnings are structurally cyclical, tied to global grain and oilseed supply-demand balances, weather, and biofuel mandate levels; the swing from a weak FY2024-2025 to a strong FY2026 illustrates this sensitivity, and the stock's post-Q3 2026 selloff shows investors pricing in cycle-peak risk.
As a working-capital- and inventory-intensive business with meaningful debt, elevated rates raise financing costs on commodity inventories and trade finance.
Significant international operations (Brazil, Europe, Asia-Pacific) expose reported results to FX translation and transaction risk, particularly the Brazilian real relative to the U.S. dollar.
Natural gas, diesel/freight, and other input costs affect processing margins across all three segments.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global agricultural processing demand continues to grow with population and biofuel mandates, but the industry remains a low-margin, high-volume business subject to cyclical swings in crop supply and government policy. Record 2026-2027 U.S. Renewable Volume Obligations remain one of the strongest policy tailwinds for the sector in years, materially lifting soybean crush margins and biodiesel/renewable diesel feedstock demand industry-wide, though management itself now flags that margins may have peaked in Q3 2026.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — earnings are strongly tied to crop harvests, crush margins, freight/logistics spreads, and biofuel policy, all of which can swing sharply quarter to quarter (illustrated by ADM's own net earnings moving from $108M in Q3 2025 to $821M in Q3 2026).
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — working capital-intensive commodity trading and processing operations mean financing costs on inventory and trade finance activities are directly affected by rate levels.
key_input_costs: Soybeans, corn, wheat, and other oilseeds/grains
Natural gas and energy for processing plants

recent_developments.event: Reported Q3 2026 results: net earnings of $821M (GAAP EPS $1.70; adjusted EPS $1.77) vs. $108M (EPS $0.22) in Q3 2025, on revenue of $22.3B (up ~10% YoY but below consensus of ~$22.7-23.3B). Total segment operating profit of $1.38B rose 64% YoY — Ag Services & Oilseeds +105% to $778M, Carbohydrate Solutions +40% to $470M (led by Vantage Corn Processors), Nutrition +3% to $134M (Animal Nutrition +21%, Human Nutrition -3% on soft liquid sweetener volumes). Wilmar equity earnings rose ~38% YoY.

ADM raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance for the third time in 2026, to approximately $5.50-$5.80 (from $5.15-$5.60 after Q2), and trimmed FY2026 capex guidance to $1.2-$1.3B (from $1.3-$1.5B). Management guided to year-over-year operating-profit improvement across all three segments in Q4 2026.

Despite the guidance raise, shares fell roughly 6.8% in the days following the Q3 print (and were down ~11.8% over the prior month per Zacks), as investors focused on CEO Juan Luciano's comment that biofuel/crush margins may have peaked for the cycle, on the revenue miss, and on how dependent the earnings beat remains on North American biofuel policy; management offered no formal 2027 guidance but described expectations for the biofuel/crush margin environment to remain historically strong into 2027.

ADM announced entry into the voluntary carbon dioxide removal market with credits from over 800,000 tons/year of carbon capture capacity at its Columbus, Nebraska corn processing complex, certified by Puro.earth under its Geologically Stored Carbon methodology.

Reported Q2 2026 net earnings of $908M (adjusted $895M), EPS of $1.87 ($1.84 adjusted); raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.15-$5.60 (from $4.15-$4.70), citing crush margin strength, biofuels tailwinds, and a 51% YoY jump in Nutrition operating profit led by record Asia-Pacific flavor sales.
ADM announced a $103M investment to modernize its Decatur, Illinois corn and soybean processing complex, adding 50 new full-time jobs and retaining 1,000+ existing roles.

EPA announced record 2026-2027 Renewable Volume Obligations (RVOs) under the Renewable Fuel Standard — the highest biomass-based diesel mandates in the program's 20-year history — a major structural tailwind for ADM's soybean crush and biofuel feedstock business.

ADM reached a settlement with the SEC resolving its multi-year investigation into Nutrition segment accounting practices: ADM agreed to pay a $40M civil penalty (without admitting or denying wrongdoing); former executives Vince Macciocchi and Ray Young settled charges, while former CFO Vikram Luthar faces a litigated SEC fraud action alleging he directed improper inter-segment adjustments to inflate Nutrition operating profit. The DOJ closed its parallel criminal probe without charges against the company.

items.notes: Third raise of 2026, up from $5.15-$5.60 given after Q2 (which itself was raised sharply from $4.15-$4.70 after Q1). Reflects continued crush margin strength and biofuels tailwinds even as management flagged that margins may have peaked for the cycle.

Trimmed from the prior $1.3-$1.5 billion range, signaling capital discipline even amid the earnings upcycle; includes low-capital-intensity crush debottlenecking projects (roughly one-fourth the capital cost of greenfield builds).

items.target: Year-over-year improvement in all three segments
items.notes: Management guidance given alongside the Q3 2026 release; no specific dollar figures provided.

CEO Juan Luciano said on the Q3 2026 call that he expects the biofuel/crush margin environment to remain historically strong into 2027, supported by robust soybean oil/meal demand and current U.S. biofuel policy, but gave no quantitative targets.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Juan Luciano attributed the Q3 2026 beat to a 'constructive biofuels environment' and ADM's North American footprint, while cautioning that crush/biofuel margins may have already peaked for this cycle even though he expects them to stay historically elevated into 2027. Management reiterated it is monitoring macroeconomic, geopolitical, policy, and trade developments that could affect the outlook, and guided to improved year-over-year segment operating profit across Ag Services & Oilseeds, Carbohydrate Solutions, and Nutrition in Q4 2026.

bull_case: Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance has now been raised three times (most recently to $5.50-$5.80), reflecting a genuine, multi-quarter earnings recovery driven by record Renewable Volume Obligations and strong crush/biofuel margins rather than a one-off beat

Diversified profit growth in Q3 2026 — Ag Services & Oilseeds +105%, Carbohydrate Solutions +40%, Wilmar equity earnings +38%, Animal Nutrition +21% — shows the recovery is broadening beyond a single segment

SEC/DOJ legal overhang substantially resolved (January 2026 $40M settlement, DOJ declined to prosecute the company), removing a multi-year cloud on the stock even though some shareholder litigation continues
Management is exercising capital discipline even in the upcycle (FY2026 capex guidance trimmed to $1.2-$1.3B) while still funding low-capital-intensity, high-return crush debottlenecking projects

53+ consecutive years of dividend increases provide an income cushion while the stock trades well off recent highs following the post-Q3 2026 selloff, offering a potentially attractive entry point if biofuel margins hold into 2027 as management expects
bear_case: Management's own comment that biofuel/crush margins 'may have peaked' for the cycle, combined with the stock falling roughly 7-12% after a guidance raise, signals the market is already discounting a less favorable 2027 margin environment

Core business remains a thin-margin, highly cyclical commodity processor whose earnings can swing nearly 8x quarter-over-quarter (Q3 2025 net earnings ~$108M vs. Q3 2026 ~$821M) purely on crush-margin and policy shifts outside management's control

Heavy dependence on government biofuel policy (RVOs, 45Z credits) for a growing share of profit is a political and regulatory tail risk; no formal 2027 guidance has been given, leaving investors to rely on qualitative management commentary rather than numbers

Nutrition segment turnaround remains inconsistent — after a 51% operating-profit jump in Q2 2026, growth slowed to just 3% in Q3 2026 with Human Nutrition down ~3% on soft liquid sweetener demand — raising doubts about the durability of the post-scandal recovery story

Q3 2026 revenue missed consensus (~$22.3B vs. ~$22.7-23.3B expected) even as profit beat, a reminder that a business with essentially no pricing power can miss top-line expectations even in a strong earnings quarter
